title: Also Add Password Changing Guidelines
body:
# Improve documentation

## Link 

https://supabase.com/docs/guides/self-hosting/docker

## Describe the problem

When password is changed like for postgres in .env , It causes an error when started again `docker compose up -d` , there is no mention of fixing that or any passwd changing guidelines.

## Describe the improvement

After many hours i found out  you need to `docker compose down -v` and also `rm -rf volumes/db/data/` sometimes. Then `docker compose up -d` to change it without error.

comments.body:
I'm able to repro the error. If I changed `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` in `.env` only, running `docker compose up -d` won't start up docker, since supabase_analytics will fail with the `password authentication failed for user "supabase_admin"` error above. This would prevent me from accessing the dashboard and other services, unless I remove the database `rm -rf volumes/db/data/`. It makes sense because the database `postgres` is created `supabase_admin` having the initial password. Trying to change password in `.env` won't change the role's password in the database.

So, I tried changing `supabase_admin` password directly (as well as `postgres` role). And then, I changed the password in `.env`. This will allow you to run supabase somewhat normally. 
```
supabase/docker
⇡3% ➜ docker compose up -d

supabase/docker
⇡4% ➜ psql -h 127.0.0.1 -p 5432 -d postgres -U supabase_admin
Password for user supabase_admin:
psql (16.2 (Homebrew), server 15.1 (Ubuntu 15.1-1.pgdg20.04+1))
Type "help" for help.

postgres=# alter user supabase_admin with password 'changed_password';
ALTER ROLE
postgres=# alter user postgres with password 'changed_password';
ALTER ROLE
postgres=# \q

supabase/docker
⇡7% ➜ docker compose down


supabase/docker
⇡7% ➜ docker compose up
```

The reason why this only "somewhat" works is because the error still appears in the supabase_anlytics logs. But, it appears less (though, still frequent), and you could access other services (at least the dashboard since that's the only thing i tested). I've yet to find a way to cleanly change password :(

Confirmed that it works as the current work around
```sql
UPDATE _analytics.source_backends
SET config = jsonb_set(config, '{url}', '"postgresql://supabase_admin:$new_passwd@db:5432/postgres"', 'false')
WHERE type='postgres';
```

comments.body:
Topic: Troubleshooting PostgreSQL Password Changes in Docker Compose
Problem Description: "Password Authentication Failed" After Updating .env
When developing locally with Docker Compose, you might encounter an error like FATAL: password authentication failed for user "postgres" after changing your PostgreSQL password (e.g., POSTGRES_PASSWORD in your .env file) and then running docker compose up -d.

Why this happens:
PostgreSQL containers, when started for the first time, read environment variables like POSTGRES_PASSWORD to initialize the database and set the user's password. This database data, including the password, is then stored persistently in a Docker volume.

If you later change the password in your .env file, the already existing database instance in the volume will still be using the old password. docker compose up -d will restart the container with the new environment variable, but it won't automatically update the password within the pre-existing database. This mismatch causes the authentication error.

Solution: Guidelines for Changing PostgreSQL Passwords
To successfully update your PostgreSQL password in your local Docker Compose environment, choose one of the following methods:

Method 1: Resetting Your Local Database (Recommended for Development)

This is the simplest way to update credentials and is ideal if your local database data is not critical and can be easily re-seeded or is just for temporary testing. This method will remove all your existing data from the PostgreSQL database.

Stop and Remove All Services and Volumes:

Bash

docker compose down --volumes
This command stops all services and, importantly, removes the persistent data volume associated with PostgreSQL, deleting the old database data (and its old password).

Update Password in .env:
Open your project's .env file and change the POSTGRES_PASSWORD (and any other relevant POSTGRES_USER, POSTGRES_DB variables if you're also changing those) to your desired new value.

Restart Docker Compose:

Bash

docker compose up -d
The PostgreSQL container will now re-initialize with the new password from your updated .env file.

Method 2: Changing Password Without Losing Existing Data (Advanced)

Use this method if you have critical local development data in your PostgreSQL instance that you cannot afford to lose. This involves manually updating the password directly within the running database.

Ensure Current Password is Set in .env:
Make sure your .env file currently contains the old password that the running PostgreSQL database is still using. You'll need this to connect initially.

Start Docker Compose Services (if not running):

Bash

docker compose up -d
Access the PostgreSQL Container Shell:
First, find the name of your PostgreSQL container (e.g., using docker ps). Then, execute a shell inside it:

Bash

docker exec -it <your-postgres-container-name> bash
(Replace <your-postgres-container-name> with the actual name, e.g., supabase_db_1)

Connect to PostgreSQL CLI (psql):
Once inside the container, connect to the database. You'll typically use the postgres user and database, or supabase_admin for Supabase. You'll be prompted for the old password.

Bash

psql -U <username> -d <database_name>
(e.g., psql -U postgres -d postgres or psql -U supabase_admin -d postgres)

Change the User's Password via SQL:
Execute the following SQL command, replacing <username> and 'your_new_password_here' with your specific details:

SQL

ALTER USER <username> WITH PASSWORD 'your_new_password_here';
-- Example for the default 'postgres' user:
-- ALTER USER postgres WITH PASSWORD 'my_super_new_secure_password';
Exit psql and Container Shell:

SQL

\q
exit
Update .env with New Password:
Now, open your .env file and update POSTGRES_PASSWORD (and any other relevant variables) to match the new password you just set via SQL.

Restart Services:

Bash

docker compose restart
Your services should now connect successfully using the newly updated password.

comments.body:
```bash
#!/bin/bash

# Script to update passwords for Supabase database users
# Author: Udara Wanasinghe
# Version: 1.0

set -euo pipefail # Exit on error, undefined variables, and pipe failures

# Configuration constants
readonly SCRIPT_NAME=$(basename "$0")
readonly CONTAINER_NAME="supabase-db"
readonly DB_USER="supabase_admin"
readonly DB_PORT=5432
readonly DB_NAME="_supabase"
readonly DB_HOST="127.0.0.1"

# Color codes for output
readonly RED='\033[0;31m'
readonly GREEN='\033[0;32m'
readonly YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
readonly BLUE='\033[0;34m'
readonly GRAY='\033[0;90m'
readonly NC='\033[0m' # No Color

# Parse command line arguments
DEBUG_MODE=false
OLD_PASSWORD=""
NEW_PASSWORD=""

# Parse arguments
while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
	case $1 in
	--debug)
		DEBUG_MODE=true
		shift
		;;
	*)
		if [[ -z "$OLD_PASSWORD" ]]; then
			OLD_PASSWORD="$1"
		elif [[ -z "$NEW_PASSWORD" ]]; then
			NEW_PASSWORD="$1"
		else
			echo "Error: Too many arguments provided"
			usage
			exit 1
		fi
		shift
		;;
	esac
done

# Make variables readonly after parsing
readonly OLD_PASSWORD
readonly NEW_PASSWORD
readonly DEBUG_MODE

# Global variables
CONTAINER_IP=""
USERS_WITH_OLD_PASSWORD=""

# Function to print colored output
print_debug() {
	if [[ "$DEBUG_MODE" == "true" ]]; then
		echo -e "${GRAY}[DEBUG] ${1}${NC}"
	fi
}

print_info() {
	echo -e "${BLUE}[INFO] ${1}${NC}"
}

print_success() {
	echo -e "${GREEN}[SUCCESS] ${1}${NC}"
}

print_warning() {
	echo -e "${YELLOW}[WARNING] ${1}${NC}"
}

print_error() {
	echo -e "${RED}[ERROR] ${1}${NC}" >&2
}

# Function to display usage information
usage() {
	cat <<EOF
Usage: $SCRIPT_NAME [--debug] <old_password> <new_password>

Description:
    Updates passwords for Supabase database users that currently use the specified old password.
    
Parameters:
    old_password    Current password to search for and replace
    new_password    New password to set for matching users
    
Options:
    --debug         Enable debug output for troubleshooting
    
Examples:
    $SCRIPT_NAME old_pass123 new_secure_pass456
    $SCRIPT_NAME --debug old_pass123 new_secure_pass456
    
Notes:
    - The script will only update users that authenticate with the old password
    - All operations are performed within a database transaction
    - Password updates are verified after completion
EOF
}

# Function to validate input parameters
validate_input() {
	print_debug "Validating input parameters..."
	print_debug "Old password length: ${#OLD_PASSWORD}"
	print_debug "New password length: ${#NEW_PASSWORD}"

	if [[ -z "$OLD_PASSWORD" || -z "$NEW_PASSWORD" ]]; then
		print_error "Both old and new passwords must be provided"
		usage
		exit 1
	fi

	if [[ "$OLD_PASSWORD" == "$NEW_PASSWORD" ]]; then
		print_error "Old and new passwords cannot be the same"
		exit 1
	fi

	# Basic password validation
	if [[ ${#NEW_PASSWORD} -lt 8 ]]; then
		print_warning "New password is less than 8 characters. Consider using a stronger password."
	fi

	print_debug "Input validation completed successfully"
	echo ""
}

# Function to check if required tools are available
check_dependencies() {
	local missing_tools=()

	if ! command -v docker &>/dev/null; then
		missing_tools+=("docker")
	fi

	if ! command -v psql &>/dev/null; then
		missing_tools+=("psql")
	fi

	if ! command -v jq &>/dev/null; then
		missing_tools+=("jq")
	fi

	if [[ ${#missing_tools[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
		print_error "Missing required tools: ${missing_tools[*]}"
		print_info "Please install the missing tools before running this script"
		exit 1
	fi
}

# Function to verify container is running
verify_container_running() {
	print_info "Checking if container '$CONTAINER_NAME' is running..."

	local running_containers
	running_containers=$(docker ps --format "{{.Names}}")
	print_debug "Running containers:\n$running_containers"

	if ! echo "$running_containers" | grep -q "^$CONTAINER_NAME$"; then
		print_error "Container '$CONTAINER_NAME' is not running"
		print_info "Please start the Supabase services before running this script"
		exit 1
	fi

	print_success "Container '$CONTAINER_NAME' is running"
	echo ""
}

# Function to get container IP address
get_container_ip() {
	print_info "Retrieving container IP address..."

	local network_name
	network_name=$(docker inspect -f '{{range $k, $v := .NetworkSettings.Networks}}{{println $k}}{{end}}' "$CONTAINER_NAME")
	print_debug "Detected network name: $network_name"

	if [[ -z "$network_name" ]]; then
		print_error "Unable to determine network for container '$CONTAINER_NAME'"
		exit 1
	fi

	CONTAINER_IP=$(docker inspect "$CONTAINER_NAME" | jq -r ".[0].NetworkSettings.Networks.\"$network_name\".IPAddress" 2>/dev/null)
	print_debug "Retrieved IP from docker inspect: $CONTAINER_IP"

	if [[ -z "$CONTAINER_IP" || "$CONTAINER_IP" == "null" ]]; then
		print_error "Unable to get IP address of container '$CONTAINER_NAME'"
		exit 1
	fi

	print_success "Container IP address: $CONTAINER_IP"
	echo ""
}

# Function to get all database users
get_all_users() {
	local all_users
	all_users=$(docker exec -i "$CONTAINER_NAME" psql \
		-h "$DB_HOST" -p "$DB_PORT" -d "$DB_NAME" -U "$DB_USER" \
		-t -c "SELECT usename FROM pg_user WHERE passwd IS NOT NULL;" \
		2>/dev/null | grep -v '^$' | sed 's/^[ \t]*//;s/[ \t]*$//') || {
		print_error "Failed to retrieve database users"
		exit 1
	}

	echo "$all_users"
}

# Function to test user authentication with old password
test_user_authentication() {
	local username="$1"
	local db_url="postgresql://$username:$OLD_PASSWORD@$CONTAINER_IP:$DB_PORT/$DB_NAME"
	print_debug "Testing authentication for user '$username' with URL: postgresql://$username:***@$CONTAINER_IP:$DB_PORT/$DB_NAME"

	psql "$db_url" -c "\q" >/dev/null 2>&1
}

# Function to find users with the old password
find_users_with_old_password() {
	print_info "Searching for users with the specified old password..."

	print_info "Retrieving list of database users..."
	local all_users
	all_users=$(get_all_users)

	print_debug "Users with passwords retrieved:\n$all_users"

	local matched_users=()

	while IFS= read -r username; do
		if [[ -n "$username" ]]; then
			print_info "Testing authentication for user: $username"

			if test_user_authentication "$username"; then
				print_success "✓ Found user with old password: $username"
				matched_users+=("$username")
			else
				print_info "✗ User $username does not have the old password"
			fi
		fi
	done <<<"$all_users"

	if [[ ${#matched_users[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then
		print_warning "No users found with the specified old password"
		exit 0
	fi

	USERS_WITH_OLD_PASSWORD=$(printf '%s\n' "${matched_users[@]}")

	echo ""
	print_info "Users to be updated:"
	echo "$USERS_WITH_OLD_PASSWORD"
	echo ""
}

# Function to generate SQL commands for password updates
generate_update_sql() {
	local sql_commands=""

	while IFS= read -r username; do
		if [[ -n "$username" ]]; then
			sql_commands+="ALTER USER \"$username\" WITH PASSWORD '$NEW_PASSWORD';"$'\n'
		fi
	done <<<"$USERS_WITH_OLD_PASSWORD"

	# Update analytics backend configuration if supabase_admin password was changed
	if echo "$USERS_WITH_OLD_PASSWORD" | grep -q "supabase_admin"; then
		sql_commands+="UPDATE _analytics.source_backends SET config = jsonb_set(config, '{url}', '\"postgresql://supabase_admin:$NEW_PASSWORD@db:5432/postgres\"', false) WHERE type = 'postgres';"$'\n'
	fi

	echo "$sql_commands"
}

# Function to update passwords
update_passwords() {
	print_info "Updating passwords for matched users..."

	local sql_commands
	sql_commands=$(generate_update_sql)
	print_debug "Generated SQL commands:\n$sql_commands"

	print_debug "Executing password update transaction..."
	docker exec -i "$CONTAINER_NAME" psql \
		-h "$DB_HOST" -p "$DB_PORT" -d "$DB_NAME" -U "$DB_USER" -q \
		<<<"BEGIN; $sql_commands COMMIT;" || {
		print_error "Failed to update passwords"
		exit 1
	}

	print_success "Password update SQL executed successfully"
	echo ""
}

# Function to verify password updates
verify_password_updates() {
	print_info "Verifying password updates..."

	local auth_tests_passed=0
	local auth_tests_total=0
	local failed_users=()

	while IFS= read -r username; do
		if [[ -n "$username" ]]; then
			((auth_tests_total++)) || true
			local new_db_url="postgresql://$username:$NEW_PASSWORD@$CONTAINER_IP:$DB_PORT/$DB_NAME"

			print_info "Testing authentication for: $username"
			if psql "$new_db_url" -c "\q" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
				print_success "✓ Authentication verified for: $username"
				((auth_tests_passed++)) || true
			else
				print_warning "✗ Authentication failed for: $username"
				failed_users+=("$username")
				# This might happen due to connection restrictions, but doesn't necessarily mean the password wasn't updated
			fi
		fi
	done <<<"$USERS_WITH_OLD_PASSWORD"

	print_info "Auth tests total: $auth_tests_total, Auth tests passed: $auth_tests_passed"

	# List all updated users with their verification status
	print_success "The following users had their passwords updated:"
	while IFS= read -r username; do
		if [[ -n "$username" ]]; then
			if [[ " ${failed_users[*]} " =~ " ${username} " ]]; then
				print_warning "  ~ $username (authentication test failed - may be due to connection restrictions)"
			else
				print_success "  ✓ $username (authentication verified)"
			fi
		fi
	done <<<"$USERS_WITH_OLD_PASSWORD"

	print_success "Password update verification completed"
	echo ""
}

# Main function
main() {
	print_info "Starting Supabase database password update process..."
	print_debug "Script started with debug mode: $DEBUG_MODE"

	validate_input
	check_dependencies
	verify_container_running
	get_container_ip
	find_users_with_old_password
	update_passwords
	verify_password_updates

	print_success "Password update process completed successfully!"
}

# Run main function if script is executed directly
if [[ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" == "${0}" ]]; then
	main "$@"
fi
